title: Jonah and the Clock
premise: In the winter of 1919, Silas Almeida, a courier carrying sealed dispatches for a collapsing republic, is stranded when the mountain bridge to the coast closes with the season's first snows. Sheltering in a remote inn, they discover the dispatches name three heirs to a contested estate — and that one of them, the innkeeper's daughter Mara, is someone Silas has loved and lied to. As factions close in on the documents and the thaw will come too late for some, Silas must decide whether loyalty to a dying state or truth to the people before them matters more. In the end, Silas burns half the dispatches, gives the last berth across the pass to Mara's younger brother, and stays behind to face what truth costs.
about_author: Kestrel Amberdale is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing diplomatic correspondence from collapsed states. They write historical fiction about the small, stubborn people history forgets to record.

chapters.title: The Weight of Sealed Things
chapters.summary: Silas crosses the high country by mail coach, guarding a leather satchel of dispatches no one may open, posing as a clock repairman. POV: Silas. The emotional beat is wary competence — Silas trusts routines, not people, and notices the coachman watching the satchel too closely.

chapters.title: Bridge Out
chapters.summary: Early snow collapses the season's last crossing; the coach deposits Silas at the Halfway House inn until spring. Among the stranded guests: a quarrelsome surveyor, a silent priest, and Mara Voss, the innkeeper's daughter, whom Silas knew years ago under another name. POV: Silas. Beat: dread disguised as inconvenience.

chapters.title: What the Inn Remembers
chapters.summary: Mara recognizes Silas; old affection resurfaces alongside old wounds. Meanwhile the priest quietly asks questions about official couriers on this road. POV alternates between Silas and Mara. Beat: warmth shadowed by the fear of being truly known.

chapters.title: Three Names on Paper
chapters.summary: Curiosity wins: Silas breaks protocol and reads the dispatches, discovering they designate heirs to the Voss family's seized estate — Mara among them — and order the estate liquidated to fund a fleeing government. POV: Silas. Beat: guilt curdling into resolve; the secret now has faces.

chapters.title: The Surveyor's Offer
chapters.summary: The surveyor reveals he knows what Silas carries and offers safe passage over the pass in exchange for the satchel — for himself, or whoever pays him. POV: Silas. Beat: temptation and the first explicit threat; loyalty begins to feel like a currency.

chapters.title: Clockwork Confessions
chapters.summary: Repairing the inn's heirloom clock with Mara, Silas almost confesses everything; instead they share a night that makes the coming betrayal worse. The priest is found copying something in the chapel. POV: Mara. Beat: love deepening precisely as deception becomes untenable.

chapters.title: The Priest's Truth
chapters.summary: The priest confronts Silas: he serves the heirs' rivals and offers protection for all if the dispatches reach him unopened. Silas refuses, but the priest hints the government already considers its couriers expendable. POV: Silas. Beat: disillusionment — duty revealed as abandonment.

chapters.title: Satchel and Snow
chapters.summary: The satchel vanishes; suspicion tears the inn apart. Mara finds it hidden in the clock case — placed there by her own brother Tomas, who read enough to learn he is an heir too. POV: Mara. Beat: family fracturing; every character now wants something from the same paper.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: A rescue sleigh arrives with room for one before the pass seals entirely. The surveyor forces a standoff; the priest lies dying from the cold he chased Silas through. Silas must choose who rides out — and chooses Tomas, giving the boy his coat and his name as escort. POV: Silas. Beat: climax — sacrifice made concrete, love expressed as loss.

chapters.title: What Burns, What Stays
chapters.summary: Silas burns the pages naming Mara, keeping only blank seals, and tells her the whole truth at last. Spring opens the road; Silas walks back toward a capital that will court-martial an empty-handed courier, while Mara watches from the bridge with the clock ticking behind her. POV: alternating, closing on Mara. Beat: bittersweet resolution — truth chosen over safety, love chosen over inheritance.
